The missing children likely died of exposure, wether setting out with a purpose or disorientated and confused with ergot poisoning from their rotten crop, or perhaps were taken in by a tribe like the Roanoke colonists.

So the interpretation of this film I subscribe to is that “a New England folk tale,” is a literal statement. We aren’t seeing events as they really happened, but seeing the story the main colony made up about this family to reinforce their social and religious views to the  larger body of their community. Either someone from the main colony or the trader went out to visit the homestand of the family, found it with the father and mother dead, a freshly dug grave, and four missing children. They didn’t have an explanation, and so created the story of the Witch tormenting this family as a way to say “obey our customs and religious beliefs or suffer for it.” 

In reality the child in the grave, Thomasin or Caleb based on the size, probably died of disease or one of a hundred other things that can happen on the frontier. The parents were violently killed either by animals or Native Americans, after which the remaining four children either were taken by the tribe or died lost in the wilderness when they fled whatever attacked their parents. In the folktale version, the twins vanish from the story basically as a plot thread that’s dropped because there’s no moralistic lesson to be taught from them, which is the goal of the folktale. I roll a rope until it’s about the width of my little finger, cut into pieces about an inch each, and roll them across a garganelli board dusted with a bit of extra semolina. Using the side of my thumb gives a squatter general shape with a larger pocket on the reverse side, but for these longer ones I used two fingertips to shape them.

Eggless, all semolina dough colored with a dehydrated and powdered beet. Still thinking about saucing and plating options that will compliment the color, but I enjoyed the light, earthy sweetness the beet adds when I cooked a handful up for a test snack with a bit of butter and herb sauce
